extracted.intended_audience: communication scholars, media researchers, and journalists interested in how online audience metrics affect news selection
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating how newspapers choose which stories to publish or follow up on in the digital age, comparing traditional professional/editorial norms with selection driven by online audience metrics (clicks/pageviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience clicks / pageviews as a selection metric
rubrics_metrics.description: On newspaper websites, journalists can observe the preferences of the audience in unprecedented detail and for low costs, based on the audience clicks (i.e. page views) for specific news articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article reports that storylines of the most-viewed articles were more likely to receive attention in subsequent reporting, which indicates that audience clicks affect news selection. Implies a criterion: higher pageviews/clicks increase likelihood of follow-up or prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional norms (editorial standards) governing news selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors consider the use of [audience click] information for news selection to conflict with professional norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on interviews with editors the study finds a normative resistance to catering to audience metrics; professional norms serve as an evaluative standard that may oppose data-driven selection even when metrics are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popularity-driven storyline propagation (newsworthiness via subsequent attention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Storylines of the most-viewed articles were more likely to receive attention in subsequent reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study's cross-lagged analysis over six months treats subsequent reporting attention as an outcome metric for news selection, suggesting 'storyline momentum' or prior popularity can be used as an indicator of newsworthiness in editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effectiveness and granularity of digital audience data
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists can observe the preferences of the audience in unprecedented detail and for low costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The availability of fine-grained, low-cost audience metrics is an implicit practical criterion for newsrooms when considering whether to incorporate metrics into selection processes; this practical affordance may push behavior even if it conflicts with professional norms.
